claim:
For every real \(\lambda>0\), let \(Z_{1,\infty}^{(\lambda)}\) be \(\mathbb R^2\) with
\[
N_\lambda(x,y)=\left(\|(x,y)\|_1^2+\lambda\|(x,y)\|_\infty^2\right)^{1/2}.
\]
Put
\[
M_\lambda=\frac{\lambda+2+\sqrt{\lambda^2+4}}2,
\qquad
m_\lambda=
\begin{cases}
1+\lambda,&0<\lambda\le2,\\
(\lambda+4)/2,&\lambda\ge2.
\end{cases}
\]
Then
\[
C_{\mathrm{Pt}}\!\left(Z_{1,\infty}^{(\lambda)}\right)
=
d_{\mathrm{BM}}\!\left(Z_{1,\infty}^{(\lambda)},\ell_2^2\right)^2
=
\frac{M_\lambda}{m_\lambda}.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
C_{\mathrm{Pt}}\!\left(Z_{1,\infty}^{(\lambda)}\right)
=
\begin{cases}
\dfrac{\lambda+2+\sqrt{\lambda^2+4}}{2(1+\lambda)},&0<\lambda\le2,\\[2mm]
\dfrac{\lambda+2+\sqrt{\lambda^2+4}}{\lambda+4},&\lambda\ge2.
\end{cases}
\]
This is exactly the published Jordan--von Neumann constant of the same family, so
\[
C_{\mathrm{Pt}}\!\left(Z_{1,\infty}^{(\lambda)}\right)
=
d_{\mathrm{BM}}\!\left(Z_{1,\infty}^{(\lambda)},\ell_2^2\right)^2
=
C_{\mathrm{NJ}}\!\left(Z_{1,\infty}^{(\lambda)}\right)
\qquad(\lambda>0).
\]
integrity: The directional comparison is exhaustive by signed-permutation symmetry, the Banach--Mazur optimum is certified by symmetry averaging over arbitrary quadratic forms, and explicit symbolic Ptolemy triples attain the comparison bound in both parameter regimes. No numerical sampling is used for the theorem.
scientific_limitations: The result is restricted to the real two-dimensional cross-exponent endpoint p=1, q=infinity of the mixed Z_{p,q} family. It does not classify the interior region 1<p<2<q<infinity. Literature coverage is bounded by the inspected primary sources and targeted searches.
title: Exact Ptolemy and Euclidean distortion of the cross-exponent \(Z_{1,\infty}\) family
